bottleneck: Editing livestock embryos produces mosaic animals where the edit is unevenly distributed, complicating breeding of true homozygous lines across generations. Off-target edits in food animals raise food-safety questions regulators have barely addressed, and public acceptance of edited meat and milk lags behind the technology. Each species needs bespoke editing and reproductive protocols, so progress in pigs does not transfer to cattle or poultry, multiplying the work.
current_state: Edited pigs (virus resistance) and cattle (heat tolerance, hornlessness) exist as research herds. Commercial deployment is limited to a few jurisdictions with permissive frameworks.

title: Livestock editing stalled by mosaicism and acceptance
why_it_blocks: Disease-resistant, climate-hardy livestock could transform food security, but mosaic founders, regulatory limbo, and consumer rejection keep edited animals in research barns instead of on farms.
